[spoiler=Pirabad-Baldullah relations][quote=pirabad;61209823]The Government of [nation]Pirabad[/nation] has confirmed that it will be sending a delegation of international observers to monitor the upcoming elections in [nation]Baladullah[/nation]. This step reflects Pirabads longstanding commitment to supporting transparent and credible democratic processes in the region.

Pirabad has repeatedly expressed its desire to strengthen cultural and economic cooperation with Baladullah, emphasizing the shared values and heritage between the two Muslim-majority nations. The participation of our observers is intended to reinforce friendship, mutual understanding, and continued collaboration in trade, education, and regional development.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reiterates that Pirabad seeks to expand relations based on respect, trust, and long-term partnership.

Mahmoud Nezami
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Pirabad[/quote]

[b]Ministry of Foreign Affairs[/b]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم[/i]

We appreciate the sending of the observer delegation, and will pay for all their expenses while they are in the country. Also, we wish to establish diplomatic, trade, and cultural ties with Pirabad as part of strengthening the unity and cooperation of the Ummah and supporting other Shamatine nations. In shaa Allah we can establish a mutually beneficial framework for cooperation in these spheres. 

Knowing that Pirabad has only recently established stability, we are also willing and able to assist your development and security against any possible remaining internal threats, in shaa Allah. 

[i]Abdoul Mahonomayi 
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Islamic Sultanate of Baladullah[/i][/spoiler]

[u]2027 Elections Info[/u]

When: [in real life, this Friday, I forget what that is in the RP lol]

Positions being contested: Sultan (new Sultan will also be able to choose to retain the current cabinet, reshuffle cabinet portfolios, or bring entirely new people on board for the heads of ministries); as Masud al-Ayyubi has served the entirely of his 3 permitted 5-year terms [first elected in 2012], there will be new people running for this position

Wazir: Current Wazir is running against an opponent

Prime Minister: Current PM is running against 2 opponents

Voting: Edit: Its actual popular vote lol

[Background info: the Sultan is the Head of State and holds primacy in the executive branch, appoints heads of ministries and departments, and can draft legislation or veto it
The Wazir is the head of the Council of Emirs and also the go-between for the Council of Emirs and the Shura Majlis, tasked with acting as a mediator when a political impasse occurs between the two
The Prime Minister is the head of the Shura Majlis and holds primacy in the legislative branch]

Candidates
Sultan: 
1. Hassan ibn Nasser al-Badawi (b. 1975, HSI) Seen as the logical successor to al-Ayyubi, he also wishes to intensify the Islamic socialist cultural revolution and deepen the role of the Quran, Sunnah, and ways of Ahl as-Sunnah Wal Jamaah (the United Community of the Prophetic Traditon, ie Orthodox Sunnism) in the Divine Law system. His father, Nasser al-Badawi (1940-2022) was a fighter against the military dictatorship during the Baladullah Civil War (1956-1977) and a learned Islamic scholar. Hassan himself is a professor of Tafsir and Quranic Arabic at the Islamic University of Madinah al-Islam. 

2. Zayd al-Shaykhani (b. 1962, HJB) As a leading figure in a party that is typically considered to want to abolish the position of Sultan, he might seem to be running for the wrong position. But he represents the Moderate wing of the HJB, which only wants to reduce the power and authority of the Sultan and give the Grand Majlisi more power. As well as being a representative for the HJB in the Grand Majlisi, he is also a part time librarian. 

Wazir:
1. Amr ibn Ubaydullah al-Haqqi (b. 1983, HAI) As the current President of the Fiqh and Shariah Department of the Ansar Islamic College, Amr is also a Shaykh and the former imam of the Grand Masjid of Maghlaba (2008-2015). His recent specialty has been on developing and codifying rules and regulations related to Islamic socialism, and he wishes to further expand and deepen the Islamic socialist revolution. 

2. Hussein Zuhraini (b. 1967, HWA) While the National Decentralization Movement party he belongs to is generally seen as a political oddity, with only 10 members in the Shura Majlis, there has been increased support for this party in Maghlaba over the past couple years, as political opposition to the NSF increases there. He is currently an accountant at a small branch of the National Bank of Baladullah, and wishes to implement a fully federal system, with greater autonomy for different provinces and a greater role for neighborhood, village, and town councils in governance. 

PM:
1. Mahmoud ibn al-Arabiyya (b. 1961, HSI)Before being the PM, he was a member of the Shura Majlis for the district of Amzaragh, in the southeast of the county. He supports all the current policies of the government and also wishes to deepen the Islamic socialist revolution. 

2. Moshe ben Haktiva (b. 1965, HTY)A Torah scholar, former grocery store owner, and avowed anti-Zionist, he is in favor of reforming the Divine Law system to give religious minorities more authority over their own affairs, but despite being Jewish he is supportive of the Islamic socialist revolution. 

3. Ahmed Dirie (b. 1986, JCO)As a longtime activist for Omori rights and social worker in the Omori communitys poorest areas, Dirie represents a bold new face in the political arena of Baladullah. Despite there being significant improvements for the Omori community [basically my nations version of Somalis] over the last couple decades, poverty, racism, over-policing, and marginalization are still notable issues amongst the Omori. Dirie wants to direct more money to improving the services and infrastructure in Omori communities, while forcing the average Baladullahan to address their prejudices and stereotypes they might have regarding his people. 

[/spoiler]

To His Excellency Abdoul Mahonomayi,
Minister of Foreign Affairs
Islamic Sultanate of Baladullah,

On behalf of the people and government of Pirabad, I extend my sincere appreciation for your warm message and for the gracious hospitality extended to our observer delegation. We are grateful for your willingness to cover all expenses and for the spirit of brotherhood and cooperation reflected in your words.

We wish the people of Baladullah peace, stability, and success in the upcoming elections, and we pray that the process brings prosperity and unity to your nation. Our convoy will include the Minister of Agriculture and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Pirabad, who will be honored to observe the elections and, if your schedule permits, engage in discussions with the appropriate representatives of your government.

In this regard, we would welcome the opportunity to explore the establishment of formal diplomatic representation. Pirabad is prepared to offer the opening of an embassy of the Islamic Sultanate of Baladullah in Shanbe, the capital of Pirabad, as a step toward deepening diplomatic, economic, and cultural cooperation between our two Muslim-majority nations. We believe such a move would greatly strengthen ties within the Ummah and lay the foundation for long-term partnership.

We thank you once again for your hospitality, goodwill, and readiness to support Pirabad during its period of rebuilding. May Allah guide our nations toward cooperation, stability, and shared prosperity.

With highest respect,
Amir-ali Attari
President
Republic of Pirabad
